question: After resolving the current-main conflicts, should this replacement land with focused runner/Codex proof, or should maintainers require live Codex/WhatsApp wedge proof first?
rationale: The code path is a narrow bug fix, but it changes lane ownership timing for plugin-owned Codex attempts and the live branch is not currently mergeable, so automation should not decide the proof/risk threshold alone.

options.title: Resolve Conflicts And Accept Focused Proof
options.body: Rebase or resolve the dirty head while preserving newer abort handling and the PR's timeout-release hooks, then merge after required checks pass.

options.title: Require Live Wedge Proof
options.body: Pause until a live or Crabbox Codex app-server wedge shows that late cleanup does not corrupt session state or user-visible delivery.

options.title: Pause The Replacement
options.body: Keep the PR open but stop automerge if maintainers want a fresh replacement branch that starts from current main.

recommendation.title: Resolve Conflicts And Accept Focused Proof
recommendation.body: Rebase or resolve the dirty head while preserving newer abort handling and the PR's timeout-release hooks, then merge after required checks pass.
